newsitem.title: USA: KANSAS HARVESTS BIGGEST-EVER WINTER WHEAT CROP.
newsitem.headline: KANSAS HARVESTS BIGGEST-EVER WINTER WHEAT CROP.

text.p: Kansas harvested its biggest-ever winter wheat crop in 1997, the state's agricultural statistics service said Tuesday after the release of the U.S. Department of Agriculture's August crop report.
USDA's report pegged total Kansas winter wheat production at 492.2 million bushels. That was about 20 million bushels above the previous record of 472 million set in 1990.

"For Kansas itself, wheat production is up 10 percent from (USDA's July report) and 93 percent above the 1996 crop," said Ron Stitzman, agricultural statistician at Kansas Agricultural Statistics in Topeka.
Stitzman said the state's crop also posted a record high yield of 46 bushels per acre (bpa), surpassing the previous record high yield of 41.5 bpa in 1983.
"The yield was up four bushels from the July 1 forecast and 17 (bpa) above a year ago," Stitzman said.
Confirmation of the state's record harvest came just months after many experts thought the crop size would be severely cut by a late spring freeze.
But the crop was rescued by a cool, extended spring, Stitzman said.
USDA also pegged Kansas corn production at 351 million bushels, which Stitzman said would be second only to last year's record high for the state of 357.2 million bushels.
Kansas soybean output was estimated at 73.6 million bushels, down slightly from the 1996 record of 74 million bushels, Stitzman said.
